title: Newport HT70 Plus Ventilator - Battery Not Charging or Shortened Runtime
description: Troubleshooting battery not charging, rapid drain, or short runtime issues on the Newport HT70 Plus ventilator.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If the ventilator is in use, immediately transition the patient to a backup ventilator before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Disconnect AC power and observe battery behavior to determine if the unit shuts off, runs briefly, or alarms.

steps.title: Check AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Reconnect AC power, verify outlet functionality, and confirm the ventilator powers on normally.

steps.title: Inspect Power Cord and Adapter
steps.instructions: Check the AC cord and power supply for damage and ensure all connections are secure.

steps.title: Confirm Charging Indicators
steps.instructions: Observe display indicators for charging status and absence of related alarms.

steps.title: Allow Adequate Charging Time
steps.instructions: Leave the ventilator connected to AC power long enough for the battery to recover and begin charging.

steps.title: Perform a Battery Runtime Check
steps.instructions: Disconnect AC power after charging and monitor runtime to verify battery capacity.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Compartment
steps.instructions: Check battery seating, contacts, and condition for corrosion, debris, or damage.

steps.title: Check for Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: Ensure the ventilator is used within proper temperature ranges to avoid battery performance issues.

CCR.Complaint: Ventilator battery not charging and unit shuts off when unplugged.
CCR.Cause: Battery failed to hold charge after full charging cycle.
CCR.Resolution: Removed ventilator from service and sent for battery replacement.

title: Newport HT70 Plus Ventilator - Circuit Leak or Disconnection Alarms
description: Troubleshooting circuit leak or disconnection alarms caused by tubing issues, loose connections, accessories, or setup problems affecting ventilation integrity.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Immediately assess the patient. If ventilation is compromised, switch to a backup ventilator or manual ventilation (BVM). Expected: Patient remains safely ventilated Why it matters: Circuit leaks can result in inadequate ventilation and patient harm

steps.title: Verify the Reported Alarm
steps.instructions: Observe the ventilator and confirm: “Circuit Leak” or “Disconnect” alarm present When the alarm occurs (startup, during breath delivery, intermittently) Expected: Alarm is reproducible or clearly observed Why it matters: Confirms a true system-detected issue vs transient event

steps.title: Check Patient Circuit Connections (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Inspect the entire breathing circuit: Ensure circuit is fully connected from ventilator to patient interface Check wye, exhalation valve, and patient connection points Reseat all connections firmly Expected: Tight, secure connections throughout Why it matters: Loose fittings are the most frequent cause of leak/disconnect alarms

steps.title: Inspect for Visible Leaks or Damage
steps.instructions: Check tubing and components for: Cracks, holes, or tears Disconnected or partially seated tubing Damaged fittings or connectors If damage is found, replace the circuit. Expected: No visible leaks or compromised components Why it matters: Even small leaks can trigger alarms and reduce delivered volume

steps.title: Check Patient Interface (ET Tube / Mask / Tracheostomy)
steps.instructions: Ensure ET tube cuff is properly inflated (if applicable) Check mask seal if using non-invasive ventilation Verify trach connections are secure Expected: Proper seal at patient interface Why it matters: Patient-side leaks are common and often overlooked

steps.title: Inspect Exhalation Valve Assembly
steps.instructions: Ensure exhalation valve is properly installed and seated Check for contamination, moisture, or improper assembly Reseat or replace if needed Expected: Valve is clean, properly seated, and functioning Why it matters: Improper valve function can mimic circuit leaks

steps.title: Check Flow Sensor and Proximal Sensor Lines (If Equipped)
steps.instructions: Ensure sensor tubing is connected and not kinked Inspect for moisture buildup or blockage Replace or dry components if needed Expected: Accurate flow measurement without obstruction Why it matters: Faulty readings can trigger false leak alarms

steps.title: Run Pre-Use Check / Leak Test
steps.instructions: Perform the ventilator’s built-in circuit check or leak test. Expected: Leak test passes within acceptable limits Why it matters: Confirms system integrity outside of patient factors

steps.title: Swap with Known Good Circuit (Isolation Step)
steps.instructions: Replace the entire circuit with a known good setup. Expected: Alarm resolves with new circuit Why it matters: Quickly isolates circuit-related issues vs ventilator fault

CCR.Complaint: Ventilator alarming “circuit leak” during patient ventilation.
CCR.Cause: Loose connection found at exhalation valve assembly causing system leak.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and secured connections; verified operation with leak test passed.

helpfulDetails: Patient interface type (ET tube, mask, trach)
Any moisture found in circuit or sensors
Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Newport HT70 Plus Ventilator - Flow Sensor Calibration Errors
description: Troubleshooting flow sensor calibration failures, inaccurate readings, or alarms caused by setup issues, contamination, or environmental factors.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the ventilator from active patient use if calibration is required and transition the patient to a backup ventilator.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Run the flow sensor calibration and observe for failure, error messages, or inconsistent readings.

steps.title: Check Circuit and Patient Setup (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Disconnect the circuit, ensure no kinks or occlusions, and remove inline accessories.

steps.title: Inspect Flow Sensor and Connections
steps.instructions: Check sensor seating, damage, and moisture; reseat securely.

steps.title: Check for Moisture or Contamination (Very Common)
steps.instructions: Inspect for condensation or debris, replace disposable parts, and dry reusable components.

steps.title: Ensure Proper Calibration Conditions
steps.instructions: Disconnect from patient, ensure proper setup, and eliminate environmental airflow interference.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Ventilator
steps.instructions: Turn off the unit, wait 30 seconds, power back on, and retry calibration.

steps.title: Verify Use of Correct Accessories
steps.instructions: Confirm only compatible circuits and sensors are being used.

steps.title: Attempt Calibration with Known Good Setup
steps.instructions: Swap in a known good sensor and circuit to isolate the issue.

CCR.Complaint: Ventilator displaying flow sensor calibration error and failing calibration.
CCR.Cause: Moisture found in flow sensor and circuit causing inaccurate readings.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced circuit and dried sensor; calibration completed successfully.

helpfulDetails: Calibration success or failure after steps

title: Newport HT70 Plus Ventilator - Pre-Use Check Failures
description: Troubleshooting pre-use check failures caused by circuit setup, leaks, sensors, or configuration issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not use the ventilator on a patient if it fails pre-use check. Move the patient to a verified working ventilator if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Run the pre-use check and observe the exact failure message or step and when it occurs during the sequence.

steps.title: Inspect Patient Circuit Setup (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Check correct circuit type, ensure all tubing is connected, verify no missing components, and reseat all connections.

steps.title: Check for Circuit Leaks
steps.instructions: Inspect for loose fittings, cracked tubing, and poorly seated components. Replace with a known-good circuit if needed.

steps.title: Verify Flow Sensor Installation and Condition
steps.instructions: Confirm correct orientation, ensure it is clean and dry, fully seated, and swap with a known-good sensor if available.

steps.title: Check Exhalation Valve Function (if applicable)
steps.instructions: Inspect for proper placement, damage, obstruction, and ensure it is clean and functioning.

steps.title: Confirm Proper Test Setup (No Patient Connected)
steps.instructions: Ensure circuit is properly configured, no patient is connected, and a test lung is used if required.

steps.title: Check Internal Settings and Mode Configuration
steps.instructions: Verify correct circuit type, proper ventilation mode, and ensure no alarm limits interfere with testing.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Ventilator
steps.instructions: Turn the unit off, wait 10–15 seconds, power it back on, and rerun the pre-use check.

CCR.Complaint: Ventilator failed pre-use check and would not pass system test.
CCR.Cause: Leak identified in patient circuit due to loose connection at flow sensor.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated connections, replaced circuit, and confirmed unit passed pre-use check successfully.

helpfulDetails: Pre-use check failure step (leak test, calibration, pressure test)

title: Newport HT70 Plus Ventilator - Alarm Not Triggering or Misconfigured
description: Addresses missing, delayed, or incorrect alarm activation due to configuration, settings, or external setup issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions:
If alarms are not functioning properly, immediately move the patient to a backup ventilator.

Expected: Patient remains safely ventilated with active alarm protection
Why it matters: Alarm failure removes a critical safety layer for detecting patient distress

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions:
Power on the ventilator and observe alarm behavior.

Check:
- Are alarms not sounding at all?
- Are alarms delayed or inconsistent?
- Are visual alarms present but no audible alarm?

Expected: Issue is clearly reproducible
Why it matters: Confirms true alarm failure vs misunderstanding of alarm behavior

steps.title: Check Alarm Volume and Mute Status (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions:
Inspect alarm audio settings:
- Ensure alarm volume is not set to minimum
- Confirm alarm silence/mute is not active
- Check for temporary silence timers

Expected: Audible alarms function at appropriate volume
Why it matters: Muted or minimized alarms are a frequent cause of “no alarm” complaints

steps.title: Review Alarm Limits and Settings
steps.instructions:
Check configured alarm thresholds:
- High/low pressure limits
- High/low tidal volume limits
- Apnea settings

Ensure limits are set appropriately for patient condition.

Expected: Alarm limits are within a realistic range to trigger alerts
Why it matters: Limits set too wide may prevent alarms from activating

steps.title: Trigger a Test Alarm Condition
steps.instructions:
Manually create a safe test condition (off patient):
- Disconnect circuit briefly to trigger disconnection alarm
- Simulate apnea if applicable

Expected: Alarm activates both visually and audibly
Why it matters: Confirms whether alarm system is functioning at all

steps.title: Check Alarm Indicator Functionality
steps.instructions:
Observe:
- Visual alarm indicators (lights, screen alerts)
- Audible alarm tones

If visual alarms work but no sound → likely speaker or audio issue
If neither works → possible system-level issue

Expected: Both visual and audible alarms function together
Why it matters: Helps isolate audio vs system failure

steps.title: Inspect External Accessories and Connections
steps.instructions:
Verify:
- Patient circuit properly connected
- Flow sensors and pressure lines correctly installed
- No bypassed or disconnected components

Expected: Proper connections allow accurate alarm triggering
Why it matters: Improper setup can prevent the ventilator from detecting fault conditions

steps.title: Check Power and System Status
steps.instructions:
Ensure stable power:
- Connected to AC or adequately charged battery
- No intermittent shutdowns or resets

Expected: Stable operation without power interruptions
Why it matters: Power instability can affect alarm system reliability

steps.title: Perform a System Restart
steps.instructions:
Power cycle the ventilator fully.

Expected: Alarm function returns to normal if issue was software-related
Why it matters: Clears temporary faults or configuration glitches

CCR.Complaint: Ventilator alarms not sounding during use.
CCR.Cause: Alarm volume found set to minimum and alarm limits set outside normal range.
CCR.Resolution: Adjusted alarm volume and reset alarm limits; verified proper alarm function with test condition.

helpfulDetails: Visual vs audible alarm behavior noted
Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Air/Oxygen Blender Will Not Reach the Set FiO2
description: Addresses incorrect delivered oxygen concentration caused by gas supplies, hoses, source connections, circuit conditions, settings, or oxygen-measurement problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Verify Oxygenation Support
steps.instructions: Do not continue using a ventilator that cannot reliably deliver the prescribed oxygen concentration. Transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup ventilation system. Confirm the set FiO2, displayed FiO2, and independently measured oxygen concentration when approved test equipment is available. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported and the actual oxygen-delivery discrepancy is confirmed.

steps.title: 2. Verify the Set FiO2
steps.instructions: Confirm that the oxygen concentration setting is appropriate and that no recent setting or mode change explains the reported condition. Avoid changing clinical settings merely to make a fault disappear. Expected outcome: The intended FiO2 setting is verified. If the issue resulted from an incorrect setting and proper operation is restored after correction, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Air and Oxygen Supply Connections
steps.instructions: Check both gas hoses from the ventilator to their sources. Confirm secure connections, correct gas source identification, absence of damaged fittings, and no obvious kinking or restriction. Expected outcome: Both required gas supplies are correctly connected and physically intact. Correcting a disconnected or restricted supply that restores normal FiO2 resolves the issue.

steps.title: 4. Verify External Gas Sources
steps.instructions: Confirm that the air and oxygen sources are available and functioning normally. When appropriate, compare operation on another verified source or approved gas outlet. Do not assume an internal blender problem until external supplies have been ruled out. Expected outcome: Stable external air and oxygen supplies are available. If moving to a verified supply restores normal FiO2 control, investigate the original infrastructure source rather than the ventilator.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Patient Circuit
steps.instructions: Inspect the breathing circuit for major leaks, incorrectly connected components, or unusual restrictions that could affect delivered gas measurements or ventilation. Expected outcome: The circuit is properly assembled and intact. Any external circuit problem is corrected before further testing.

steps.title: 6. Compare Set and Measured Oxygen Concentration
steps.instructions: Using approved oxygen-analysis equipment, compare delivered oxygen concentration with the ventilator setting under controlled bench conditions. Allow the system to stabilize according to approved procedures before interpreting results. Expected outcome: Delivered oxygen concentration corresponds appropriately with the selected setting. If verified output is correct, investigate the reported clinical circumstances or displayed measurement rather than assuming blender failure.

steps.title: 7. Test Across More Than One FiO2 Setting
steps.instructions: With the ventilator off-patient and connected to appropriate test equipment, verify that oxygen concentration responds when the set value is changed through representative test points allowed by your procedure. Expected outcome: Measured oxygen concentration changes predictably with commanded FiO2. If control is stable and accurate, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 8. Check for Oxygen-Sensor Contribution
steps.instructions: If independently measured oxygen concentration is correct but the ventilator display remains inaccurate, evaluate the oxygen-sensor calibration and condition using approved procedures. Expected outcome: Independent measurement and ventilator indication agree after approved sensor verification or calibration. If not, continue escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify ventilation, delivered oxygen concentration, applicable gas-supply alarms, and oxygen-monitoring response before return to service. Expected outcome: FiO2 control is stable, independent measurement agrees with expected delivery, and alarms function normally.

steps.title: 10. Escalate if FiO2 Cannot Be Controlled
steps.instructions: If stable known-good gas supplies and correct external setup do not restore oxygen control, remove the ventilator from service. Expected outcome: An unresolved oxygen-delivery problem is escalated rather than accepted for clinical use.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Newport e360 would not achieve the selected oxygen concentration.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the oxygen hose was connected to an external source that was not providing a usable oxygen supply.
CCR.Resolution: The ventilator was connected to a verified oxygen source, delivered FiO2 was confirmed with an oxygen analyzer, and ventilation and alarms passed functional testing.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Alarm Speaker or Nurse-Call Output Fails Verification
description: Addresses missing audible alarms or remote alarm signaling caused by settings, cables, connectors, destination equipment, or internal alarm-output faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Provide Alternate Alarm Coverage
steps.instructions: Do not use the ventilator clinically if required alarm annunciation cannot be trusted. Move the patient to another verified ventilator or provide an approved alternate monitoring and alarm method during evaluation. Determine whether the failure involves the local alarm speaker, nurse-call output, or both. Expected outcome: Patient alarm coverage is maintained and the failed portion of the alarm pathway is identified.

steps.title: 2. Verify Alarm Volume and Permitted Settings
steps.instructions: Review accessible alarm-volume and related settings without bypassing minimum protections or entering restricted configuration. Expected outcome: The alarm is configured appropriately. If correcting an unintended permitted setting restores audible annunciation, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Trigger a Controlled Alarm Off-Patient
steps.instructions: Connect a test lung and deliberately create an approved test condition that generates an alarm. Observe audible, visual, and remote alarm behavior. Expected outcome: The ventilator produces appropriate local visual and audible annunciation. If not, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Alarm Speaker Path Externally
steps.instructions: Check that speaker openings are not physically blocked by labels, covers, debris, or accessories. Listen for distorted, intermittent, or unusually faint output. Expected outcome: The speaker path is unobstructed and audible output is clear. Persistent speaker failure requires escalation.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Nurse-Call Cable
steps.instructions: If remote output is the problem, inspect the nurse-call cable, plug, adapter, and ventilator connection for damage or incomplete seating. Expected outcome: The cable and connector are intact and firmly connected.

steps.title: 6. Substitute a Known-Good Nurse-Call Cable
steps.instructions: When available, use a verified compatible cable or adapter. Expected outcome: The remote alarm operates with the known-good cable. If so, replace the defective accessory and proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 7. Verify the Receiving System
steps.instructions: Test the nurse-call or remote alarm input independently according to facility procedures, or connect the ventilator to a known-good receiving input. Coordinate with the appropriate communications or facilities team when required. Expected outcome: The receiving infrastructure accepts a verified alarm input. If the infrastructure is defective, route the issue to the responsible department.

steps.title: 8. Verify the Complete Alarm Path
steps.instructions: Generate an approved ventilator alarm and confirm the local audible alarm, local visual indication, cable output, receiving station, and final annunciation point. Expected outcome: The complete alarm pathway functions reliably from ventilator to receiving destination.

steps.title: 9. Repeat the Test
steps.instructions: Repeat alarm activation to identify intermittent connections or output failures. Expected outcome: Local and remote alarm functions operate consistently on repeated testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Alarm Failure
steps.instructions: If the speaker or output remains unreliable with known-good external equipment, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service for service-level evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that alarms sounded at the Newport e360 but were not reaching the nurse-call system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external nurse-call cable had an intermittent connection at the ventilator plug.
CCR.Resolution: The cable was replaced, repeated alarm tests reached the receiving station correctly, and local audible and visual alarms were also verified.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Disconnect Alarm Is Delayed or Triggers With an Intact Circuit
description: Addresses inappropriate disconnect-alarm behavior caused by circuit leaks, alarm settings, sensing problems, accessories, patient-interface simulation, or circuit configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Provide Reliable Alarm Coverage
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable disconnect alarm while a patient depends on the ventilator. Transfer the patient to another verified ventilator or provide appropriate backup ventilation and alarm coverage. Determine whether the alarm is delayed during an actual disconnect, activates without a disconnect, or behaves intermittently. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and the exact alarm behavior is reproduced off-patient.

steps.title: 2. Review Alarm Settings
steps.instructions: Verify accessible disconnect-related alarm settings and associated pressure or volume alarm parameters without changing clinical safeguards simply to suppress the complaint. Expected outcome: Settings are appropriate for the intended test. If an inadvertent setting explains the behavior, correct it and continue to final verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Complete Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check the inspiratory limb, expiratory limb, humidification components, filters, adapters, test lung connection, and exhalation components for loose fittings, leaks, obstructions, or incorrect assembly. Expected outcome: The circuit is complete and intact. Correcting an actual leak that stops false disconnect alarms resolves the issue after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Excessive Compliance or Unusual Accessories
steps.instructions: Identify added tubing, adapters, filters, or other components that differ from the usual setup and could affect pressure or flow behavior. Expected outcome: The circuit setup is appropriate and does not contain an unintended accessory or configuration contributing to alarm behavior.

steps.title: 5. Verify Exhalation and Flow-Sensing Components
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible exhalation and flow-sensing components for proper installation, moisture, contamination, or loose connections. Expected outcome: Sensing-related external components are clean, dry, and correctly installed.

steps.title: 6. Perform a Controlled Disconnect Test
steps.instructions: Using a test lung and approved procedure, create a deliberate circuit disconnect and observe alarm detection. Do not use a patient as the test load. Expected outcome: The ventilator detects the disconnect and annunciates according to manufacturer-defined behavior.

steps.title: 7. Test for False Alarm Conditions
steps.instructions: Reconnect the circuit securely and allow ventilation to stabilize. Observe whether the disconnect alarm activates despite an intact circuit. Expected outcome: No disconnect alarm occurs with a correctly assembled, leak-free test circuit.

steps.title: 8. Substitute Known-Good Circuit Components
steps.instructions: If false alarms persist, substitute a known-good circuit, test lung, and compatible sensing accessories as appropriate. Expected outcome: Normal alarm behavior with known-good components identifies an external circuit or accessory as the cause.

steps.title: 9. Perform Complete Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Verify disconnect-related alarms along with related pressure or volume alarms under controlled conditions. Expected outcome: Alarm detection is reliable and repeatable during intentional fault conditions and remains inactive during normal ventilation.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Unresolved Alarm Behavior
steps.instructions: If known-good external components and appropriate settings do not restore reliable disconnect detection, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service for further evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported repeated disconnect alarms from the Newport e360 even though the patient circuit appeared connected.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found a loose circuit adapter creating an intermittent leak during ventilation.
CCR.Resolution: The adapter was replaced and secured, intentional disconnect testing and intact-circuit testing were completed successfully, and related alarms were verified.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Event Log, Trend, or Serial Communication Export Fails
description: Addresses missing event, trend, or serial data caused by cables, ports, receiving systems, communication settings, configuration, or export-media problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Operation Before Troubleshooting Data Functions
steps.instructions: Do not interrupt active patient ventilation solely to troubleshoot data export or serial communications. If testing could affect ventilation, remove the ventilator from patient use first. Clarify whether the problem involves event logs, trend retrieval, serial output, external monitoring, or export to another system. Expected outcome: Ventilation remains uninterrupted and the failed data path is clearly identified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Data Exists Locally
steps.instructions: Review accessible event or trend information on the ventilator without entering restricted service functions. Expected outcome: The requested information is present locally. If no data exists for the requested period, the issue is not an export-path failure.

steps.title: 3. Inspect External Communication Connections
steps.instructions: Check the communication cable, connectors, adapters, and externally accessible port for loose connections, bent contacts, damage, or strain. Expected outcome: Connections are secure and physically intact. Reseating a loose cable that restores communication resolves the issue after verification.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Correct Port and Cable Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the cable and port being used are intended for the required communication function and are approved for the ventilator and receiving equipment. Expected outcome: The correct communication path is being used.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Cable or Adapter
steps.instructions: When available, test with a known-good compatible communication cable or adapter. Expected outcome: Communication is restored with the known-good accessory. If so, replace the defective external cable or adapter.

steps.title: 6. Verify Permitted Communication Settings
steps.instructions: Review accessible serial or communication settings against the documented requirements of the connected system. Do not change protected service configuration without authorization and documentation. Expected outcome: Both ends of the connection are configured to communicate using compatible documented settings.

steps.title: 7. Test the Receiving Device or System
steps.instructions: Verify that the destination computer, interface, monitoring system, or serial converter is operating normally. Test its input using another verified source when possible. Expected outcome: The receiving system is available and able to accept data. If not, escalate the infrastructure or integration issue to the responsible support team.

steps.title: 8. Isolate the Ventilator From the Network or Integration Path
steps.instructions: Where applicable, test direct local communication using approved equipment to determine whether the failure is at the ventilator or farther downstream. Expected outcome: Direct communication works if the ventilator output is functional. A failure beyond that point identifies an external infrastructure issue.

steps.title: 9. Verify Event or Trend Export
steps.instructions: Repeat the required export and confirm that the received data is complete, correctly associated, and readable. Expected outcome: Requested event, trend, or serial data transfers successfully and consistently.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Ventilator Functional Verification
steps.instructions: If the ventilator was removed from service or restarted during troubleshooting, verify normal ventilation, controls, alarms, and communication before return to service. Expected outcome: Ventilator operation remains normal and the communication function is restored.

steps.title: 11. Escalate Persistent Communication Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good cables, correct permitted configuration, and a verified receiving device do not resolve communication, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The problem is routed for qualified service or integration support without unauthorized internal repair.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that event data from the Newport e360 would not transfer to the connected receiving system.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external serial communication cable had a damaged connector and failed when tested against a known-good cable.
CCR.Resolution: The communication cable was replaced, event data exported successfully to the receiving system, and normal ventilator operation was verified.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Exhalation Valve Calibration or Leak Test Fails
description: Addresses failed exhalation-valve calibration or circuit leak testing caused by circuit setup, valve assembly, connections, accessories, or external leakage.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm the Reported Failure
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot the ventilator while a patient depends on unreliable ventilation. Move the patient to another verified ventilator or appropriate backup ventilation method before testing. Confirm whether the reported problem is an exhalation-valve calibration failure, circuit leak-test failure, or both. Record any displayed message exactly as shown. Expected outcome: The patient is safely supported elsewhere and the exact failed test or symptom is identified. If the problem cannot be reproduced and all required checks pass, troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Breathing Circuit for Obvious Leaks
steps.instructions: Inspect the inspiratory and expiratory limbs, connectors, humidification components, test lung, caps, adapters, and sampling connections. Look for loose fittings, cracks, improperly seated components, or open ports. Verify that the circuit configuration matches the intended test setup. Expected outcome: The circuit is complete, correctly connected, and visibly free of leakage. If correcting a loose or open connection allows the test to pass consistently, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after functional verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Exhalation Valve Assembly
steps.instructions: Remove the ventilator from clinical use and inspect the externally accessible exhalation valve components according to approved handling procedures. Confirm that the assembly is correctly installed, fully seated, clean, dry, and free of visible damage or contamination. Do not disassemble internal pneumatic components beyond authorized service procedures. Expected outcome: The exhalation valve is correctly installed and unobstructed. If reseating or replacing an approved removable valve component restores successful calibration, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Moisture or Contamination
steps.instructions: Inspect the expiratory circuit and exhalation valve area for condensate, secretions, cleaning residue, or other material that could prevent proper valve movement or sealing. Replace contaminated or questionable disposable components rather than attempting unauthorized repair. Expected outcome: The gas path and valve components are clean and dry. If removing moisture or replacing a contaminated component restores the test, the problem is resolved.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Circuit or Valve Assembly
steps.instructions: When available, install a compatible known-good breathing circuit and externally replaceable exhalation valve assembly. Repeat the applicable calibration or leak check. Expected outcome: A known-good setup passes testing. If the original accessory causes the failure and the replacement passes repeatedly, replace the defective accessory and stop troubleshooting after final verification.

steps.title: 6. Verify Gas Supply and Basic Ventilator Operation
steps.instructions: Confirm that required air and oxygen supplies are connected, secure, and available to the ventilator. Verify normal startup and absence of unrelated supply or pressure alarms. Expected outcome: The ventilator has stable required gas supplies and operates normally aside from the reported issue. Correcting an external gas-supply problem that restores calibration resolves the issue.

steps.title: 7. Repeat the Calibration or Leak Test
steps.instructions: Using the correct external setup, repeat the required calibration or pre-use test. Do not bypass a failed test or alter unauthorized configuration parameters to force a pass. Expected outcome: The ventilator completes the test successfully and consistently. If it does, proceed to final functional verification.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Connect an appropriate test lung and verify basic ventilation, exhalation, pressure behavior, volume response, and applicable alarms using approved test equipment and procedures. Expected outcome: Ventilation and alarms function normally with no abnormal leakage or calibration failure. The ventilator may be returned to service only after required testing is successfully completed.

steps.title: 9. Escalate if the Failure Remains
steps.instructions: If known-good external components and correct setup do not resolve the problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service for manufacturer-directed evaluation rather than being returned to clinical use with an unresolved calibration or leak-test failure.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the Newport e360 repeatedly failed the exhalation valve calibration during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the removable exhalation valve assembly was not fully seated, preventing the circuit from sealing correctly.
CCR.Resolution: The valve assembly was correctly reseated, the calibration and leak test passed, and ventilation and alarm functions were successfully verified with a test lung.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Flow Sensor Is Not Detected or Tidal-Volume Accuracy Is Out of Tolerance
description: Addresses missing flow sensing or inaccurate tidal-volume measurement caused by circuit leaks, sensor setup, contamination, connections, configuration, or calibration.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Confirm the Symptom
steps.instructions: Do not continue clinical use if tidal-volume monitoring or delivery cannot be trusted. Transfer the patient to another verified ventilator. Determine whether the problem is sensor detection, displayed tidal volume, delivered tidal volume, or a failed verification test. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and the reported measurement problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check the circuit for loose connections, leaks, incorrectly installed components, water accumulation, damaged tubing, or open sampling ports. Expected outcome: The breathing circuit is intact and correctly assembled. If correcting a circuit leak restores normal volume readings, the issue is resolved after verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Flow-Sensing Components
steps.instructions: Inspect externally accessible flow-sensing components and their connectors for contamination, moisture, physical damage, improper orientation, or incomplete seating. Do not attempt internal sensor repair. Expected outcome: The sensor and connections are clean, dry, properly installed, and undamaged.

steps.title: 4. Reseat Sensor Connections
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect approved removable sensor connections with the ventilator removed from clinical use. Check for bent contacts, damaged connectors, or poor engagement. Expected outcome: The ventilator consistently recognizes the sensor. If reseating restores detection and subsequent verification passes, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 5. Substitute a Known-Good Compatible Sensor or Circuit
steps.instructions: When available, install a verified compatible sensor or circuit component. Expected outcome: The known-good component is detected and produces stable measurements. If the fault follows the original accessory, replace it and proceed to final testing.

steps.title: 6. Verify Configuration and Circuit Type
steps.instructions: Confirm that the ventilator is configured appropriately for the circuit and accessories installed. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or alter calibration constants. Expected outcome: External setup and permitted configuration agree with the installed circuit.

steps.title: 7. Perform Approved Flow or Sensor Calibration
steps.instructions: With the ventilator off-patient, complete any user-accessible or authorized calibration required for the installed flow-sensing setup. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully. A repeated calibration failure with known-good external components requires escalation.

steps.title: 8. Measure Delivered Tidal Volume Independently
steps.instructions: Connect an approved ventilator analyzer and test lung. Compare independently measured tidal volume with the ventilator's delivered and displayed values under controlled conditions. Expected outcome: Delivered and monitored values meet the applicable manufacturer verification criteria. If they do, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 9. Check Across Representative Test Conditions
steps.instructions: Where permitted by the approved procedure, repeat volume verification using more than one controlled test setting to ensure the problem is not intermittent or condition-dependent. Expected outcome: Volume measurement remains stable and acceptable throughout testing.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Accuracy Problem
steps.instructions: If known-good circuits and sensors, proper setup, and approved calibration do not restore acceptable performance, stop troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service for further evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Newport e360 displayed inconsistent tidal volumes during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found moisture in the externally connected flow-sensing component, causing unstable measurements.
CCR.Resolution: The affected component was replaced with a verified compatible sensor, calibration passed, and tidal-volume accuracy was confirmed with a ventilator analyzer.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Internal Battery or AC/DC Power Switchover Fails
description: Addresses battery charging, backup-power, and power-source transfer problems caused by AC supply, cords, external DC sources, connections, or battery condition.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Testing Power Sources
steps.instructions: Do not deliberately disconnect power from a ventilator supporting a patient to test battery operation. Move the patient to a verified ventilator or provide suitable backup ventilation first. Confirm whether the complaint involves charging, battery operation, AC loss switchover, external DC operation, or unexpected shutdown. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and the exact power-related complaint is understood.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the AC Power Cord and Connection
steps.instructions: Check the power cord, plug, strain relief, and ventilator power inlet for visible damage, looseness, heat discoloration, or contamination. Expected outcome: The AC connection is secure and undamaged. If correcting a loose connection restores normal charging and operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Outlet
steps.instructions: Test the outlet with appropriate electrical-safety or outlet-testing equipment, or move the ventilator to a known-good approved receptacle. Expected outcome: A reliable AC source is confirmed. If the ventilator operates normally on another outlet, refer the original receptacle or branch-circuit concern to the appropriate facilities personnel.

steps.title: 4. Confirm AC Operation and Charging Indication
steps.instructions: Power the ventilator from verified AC and observe normal startup, AC status, and battery charging indications. Do not rely solely on a staff report that the unit had been plugged in. Expected outcome: The ventilator recognizes AC power and indicates expected battery charging behavior. Failure to recognize verified AC requires escalation after external connections are checked.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Any External DC Power Setup
steps.instructions: If external DC operation is part of the complaint, inspect the approved DC cable, connector, source, and any externally accessible fuse or adapter allowed by facility procedures. Use only compatible approved accessories. Expected outcome: The external DC source and cable are correctly connected and functional. A known-good approved cable or source restores operation if the original accessory was defective.

steps.title: 6. Evaluate Battery Condition
steps.instructions: With the ventilator off-patient, review the available battery status indication. Look for failure to charge, rapid depletion, inability to support operation, or an abnormal battery condition. Do not open or rebuild the battery pack. Expected outcome: The battery accepts charge and shows usable status. A battery that remains unable to support operation after verified charging should be replaced or evaluated according to approved service procedures.

steps.title: 7. Test Power Switchover Off-Patient
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate test lung and controlled bench setup, verify transfer between approved power sources according to facility and manufacturer procedures. Observe for rebooting, ventilation interruption, alarm behavior, or loss of display. Expected outcome: Ventilation continues appropriately through the tested power transition and the ventilator provides the expected power-source indication or alarm. If switchover works repeatedly, the issue is resolved.

steps.title: 8. Verify Battery Backup Function
steps.instructions: Where approved, operate the ventilator from internal battery long enough to confirm stable backup operation without making assumptions about total runtime beyond manufacturer-defined testing procedures. Expected outcome: The ventilator remains operational and stable on internal battery during the functional test.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Electrical and Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction, perform required electrical-safety testing, verify charging, confirm power-source transfer, and verify basic ventilation and alarms. Expected outcome: All tested power modes function normally with no interruption to ventilation.

steps.title: 10. Escalate an Unresolved Power Failure
steps.instructions: If known-good AC, approved DC sources, cables, and battery replacement or approved battery evaluation do not resolve the problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service rather than being used with unreliable backup power.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the Newport e360 shut down when AC power was disconnected for transport preparation.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the internal battery would not support ventilator operation despite verified AC charging.
CCR.Resolution: The battery was replaced using an approved service procedure, power switchover was verified off-patient, and ventilation and alarms passed final testing.

helpfulDetails: External DC source and cable tested

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Internal Oxygen Sensor Will Not Calibrate or FiO2 Display Drifts
description: Addresses oxygen-sensor calibration failure or drifting FiO2 indication caused by gas supplies, sensor condition, circuit setup, calibration conditions, or measurement faults.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Independently Verify Oxygen
steps.instructions: Do not rely on a questionable FiO2 display for patient management. Move the patient to a verified ventilator if oxygen measurement or delivery cannot be trusted. Use an approved external oxygen analyzer to distinguish a display problem from an actual gas-delivery problem. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and actual delivered oxygen concentration is independently known.

steps.title: 2. Compare Displayed and Measured FiO2
steps.instructions: Allow the system and external analyzer to stabilize under controlled bench conditions. Compare the ventilator display with the independent measurement. Expected outcome: The independent analyzer establishes whether the problem is actual oxygen delivery or oxygen-sensor indication.

steps.title: 3. Verify Air and Oxygen Supplies
steps.instructions: Check both gas supplies and associated hoses for secure connections and proper availability. Expected outcome: Stable gas supplies are confirmed. If an external supply problem explains the unstable reading and correcting it restores normal operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Breathing Circuit
steps.instructions: Check for major leaks, unusual adapters, incorrect setup, or other external conditions that could affect the gas mixture being sampled. Expected outcome: The circuit is correctly configured and stable.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Oxygen Sensor Externally
steps.instructions: Where the sensor is externally accessible under approved service procedures, inspect its seating, connector, age or condition information if available, and evidence of contamination or damage. Do not disassemble the sensor. Expected outcome: The sensor is properly installed and physically acceptable.

steps.title: 6. Perform Approved Oxygen-Sensor Calibration
steps.instructions: Using the required gas conditions and manufacturer-approved procedure, attempt calibration. Do not alter hidden calibration constants or bypass a failed calibration. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully and subsequent readings stabilize. If so, continue to verification.

steps.title: 7. Substitute a Known-Good Sensor When Permitted
steps.instructions: If the sensor is a qualified replaceable service item, install a compatible known-good or approved replacement sensor. Expected outcome: Calibration succeeds and displayed FiO2 agrees with independent measurement. If so, the original sensor was the cause and troubleshooting can stop after final testing.

steps.title: 8. Check for Drift Over Time
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator on a test lung and monitor displayed and independently measured FiO2 over a controlled observation period. Expected outcome: The displayed oxygen concentration remains stable and tracks independent measurement appropriately.

steps.title: 9. Verify Multiple Oxygen Settings
steps.instructions: Where permitted, compare displayed and measured oxygen concentration at more than one commanded FiO2. Expected outcome: The ventilator indicates oxygen concentration consistently across the tested range according to approved acceptance criteria.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Calibration or Drift
steps.instructions: If a verified gas supply, correct setup, approved calibration, and known-good sensor do not resolve the problem, remove the ventilator from service. Expected outcome: An unresolved oxygen-monitoring fault is escalated for service evaluation.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported that the Newport e360 FiO2 display drifted despite a stable oxygen setting.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the replaceable oxygen sensor would not maintain calibration while independent oxygen delivery remained stable.
CCR.Resolution: The oxygen sensor was replaced, calibration completed successfully, and displayed FiO2 was verified against an external oxygen analyzer.

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Nebulizer Output Is Missing or Does Not Synchronize With Inspiration
description: Addresses absent or mistimed nebulizer operation caused by setup, tubing, nebulizer accessories, settings, connections, or ventilator output problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Preserve Therapy
steps.instructions: If aerosol therapy is clinically required and the ventilator nebulizer function is unreliable, provide therapy using an approved alternate method while troubleshooting occurs off-patient. Confirm whether nebulizer output is completely absent, weak, continuous, or improperly synchronized. Expected outcome: Required therapy is maintained and the exact nebulizer fault is identified.

steps.title: 2. Verify Nebulizer Function Is Enabled Appropriately
steps.instructions: Review the accessible ventilator nebulizer controls and confirm that the feature is intentionally activated for the test. Do not alter unrelated ventilation settings simply to produce nebulizer flow. Expected outcome: Nebulizer operation is properly commanded. If the function was unintentionally disabled and normal output returns, proceed to verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Nebulizer Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Check the nebulizer gas tubing for kinks, cracks, loose connections, obstruction, or incorrect attachment. Expected outcome: The tubing is intact, correctly routed, and securely connected.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Nebulizer Device
steps.instructions: Confirm that the nebulizer cup or compatible accessory is assembled correctly and is not visibly damaged, clogged, or contaminated. Use only approved compatible accessories. Expected outcome: The external nebulizer assembly is correctly prepared and unobstructed.

steps.title: 5. Substitute Known-Good Accessories
steps.instructions: Use a compatible known-good nebulizer and tubing set when available. Expected outcome: Nebulizer output returns with the known-good accessory. If so, replace the defective external component and continue to final testing.

steps.title: 6. Observe Output Off-Patient
steps.instructions: Operate the ventilator on a test lung and activate the nebulizer function. Observe whether gas output occurs and whether aerosol generation is present. Expected outcome: The nebulizer produces consistent output when commanded.

steps.title: 7. Check Synchronization With Inspiration
steps.instructions: Observe several ventilation cycles and determine whether nebulizer output corresponds with the intended inspiratory phase behavior. Do not rely on a single cycle. Expected outcome: Nebulizer activation consistently follows the expected ventilatory timing during repeated breaths.

steps.title: 8. Check Ventilation Mode and Setup
steps.instructions: Confirm that the test conditions allow the nebulizer function to operate as expected and that the reported behavior is not related to an incompatible setup or mode limitation. Use manufacturer documentation when the expected behavior is uncertain. Expected outcome: The test setup is appropriate for evaluating nebulizer synchronization.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Verify normal ventilation, aerosol output, synchronization, and alarms after correction. Expected outcome: Nebulizer output is reliable and ventilation remains stable.

steps.title: 10. Escalate if Output Remains Absent or Mistimed
steps.instructions: If known-good external tubing and nebulizer accessories do not resolve the problem, stop external troubleshooting. Expected outcome: The ventilator is removed from service when its required nebulizer function cannot be verified.

CCR.Complaint: Respiratory Therapy reported no nebulizer output from the Newport e360 during treatment setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external nebulizer tubing kinked near the ventilator connection, preventing gas flow.
CCR.Resolution: The tubing was replaced, nebulizer output and inspiratory synchronization were verified on a test lung, and the ventilator passed functional testing.

helpfulDetails: Nebulizer output absent, weak, or continuous

title: Newport e360 Ventilator - Touchscreen, Rotary Knob, or Display Is Unresponsive
description: Addresses frozen or unresponsive controls and display problems caused by power, contamination, accessories, startup state, or control-interface failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Before Manipulating Controls
steps.instructions: If controls or the display cannot be trusted, do not troubleshoot while the ventilator supports a patient. Transfer ventilation to another verified device. Determine whether the touchscreen, rotary control, entire display, or only a specific area or function is affected. Expected outcome: The patient is protected and the exact control-interface problem is identified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Basic Power and Startup
steps.instructions: Verify that the ventilator is connected to a known-good power source and completes normal startup as far as visible. Observe whether the display is blank, frozen, partially illuminated, distorted, or operating normally while controls remain unresponsive. Expected outcome: Power is stable and the failure is isolated to the user interface rather than a complete loss of power.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Screen and Controls
steps.instructions: Check for moisture, cleaning residue, protective material, physical impact damage, cracked surfaces, stuck controls, or contamination around the touchscreen and rotary knob. Expected outcome: The interface is clean, dry, and physically unobstructed. If cleaning approved external contamination restores reliable operation, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 4. Remove External Accessories That Could Affect Operation
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external communication accessories or peripherals while the ventilator is off-patient if permitted by facility procedures. Restart the ventilator normally. Expected outcome: The ventilator starts with responsive controls. If a peripheral consistently causes the problem, isolate the accessory or integration issue.

steps.title: 5. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: With the ventilator removed from clinical use, shut it down and restart it using normal operating controls. Do not repeatedly power-cycle an unstable ventilator as a substitute for repair. Expected outcome: The interface initializes and remains responsive. If the issue returns, continue troubleshooting rather than returning the device to service.

steps.title: 6. Check Rotary Control Operation
steps.instructions: Verify that the rotary control moves freely and consistently registers permitted menu navigation and selections. Expected outcome: Rotary input corresponds with on-screen movement and selection. Erratic or absent response suggests a control-interface fault requiring escalation.

steps.title: 7. Check Touchscreen Response
steps.instructions: Test multiple areas of the touchscreen using normal non-clinical menu functions. Do not enter restricted service menus or change protected configuration. Expected outcome: Touch inputs register at the intended locations. Persistent dead areas or incorrect touch registration require service evaluation.

steps.title: 8. Observe Display Stability
steps.instructions: Allow the ventilator to operate on a test lung while observing for freezing, flickering, loss of backlighting, corrupted graphics, or delayed updates. Expected outcome: The display remains stable and controls remain responsive throughout testing.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional and Alarm Verification
steps.instructions: Verify control entry, ventilation changes under controlled bench conditions, display updates, and audible and visual alarms. Expected outcome: Controls and display are consistently responsive and ventilation responds correctly to permitted setting changes.

steps.title: 10. Escalate Persistent Interface Failure
steps.instructions: If external conditions and controlled restart do not restore reliable operation, remove the ventilator from service. Expected outcome: A ventilator with unreliable controls or display is not returned to patient use.

CCR.Complaint: Staff reported that the Newport e360 touchscreen stopped responding during pre-use setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried cleaning residue across the touchscreen surface that interfered with touch response.
CCR.Resolution: The display was cleaned using the approved method, touchscreen response was verified across the interface, and ventilation and alarm functions passed testing.
